summary: Correct Web fresh-session model authority after a Gen62 live canary proved that session.created could transiently inherit another tab's shared-current model before the same request corrected it. A valid explicit model on new_session now owns creation authority immediately; M60 shared-current inheritance remains only when the request omits model, and an explicit unknown model remains unbound for the existing per-call unavailable-routing fact.

components.owning_subsystem: Web session creation and model authority
components.disposition: ADMIT corrective authority precedence: for new_session, an explicitly supplied valid model is canonicalized before Session creation and becomes the initial model_override. If an explicit model is unknown, the session is created without a persisted override; shared-current inheritance is used only when model is absent. Existing-session authority and routing behavior are unchanged.
evidence: Gen62 live canary ef3315ca-cfdb-49a0-8ddc-5271b28140d9 recorded session.created as Qwen from another tab while the same explicit request ran/finalized as GLM
components.verification_level: deterministic concurrent-tab regression + full repository CI + post-deploy fresh-session canary
components.model_evidence_veto_recovery_exit: This changes only mechanical precedence of human Web request facts at session creation. It does not let the program choose a model semantically. Explicit unknown models remain unpersisted and continue through the existing truthful unavailable-routing path; omitted model retains the existing M60 shared-current fallback.
components.rollback_route: Revert this corrective commit; no data migration is required. If deployed, publish a new managed generation and restart affected services through service-control.

components.disposition: ADMIT regression matrix: preserve M60 no-model inheritance while proving explicit request authority wins at creation for sync/stream, reverse-tab model combinations, and invalid explicit model does not inherit unrelated shared authority.
evidence: Ruff and Pyright changed-file gates PASS
components.verification_level: focused deterministic tests + adjacent model/session regression suite

components.disposition: ADMIT mechanical architecture-review path coverage for the fresh-session model-authority correction.

g1.necessity: A live concurrent-tab canary proved session.created could record another tab's shared-current model before the explicit model on the same new-session request was applied, violating authoritative creation metadata and session-local model ownership.

g2.authority_owner: The explicit model fact on the Web new_session request, canonicalized against the current model registry
g2.non_duplication: This replaces only the creation-time precedence that previously always consulted process-global shared_current. It reuses the existing canonical model resolver and existing M60 inheritance fallback rather than adding a parallel model authority store.

model_evidence: live ef3315ca session.created=Qwen followed by request.meta/transport/usage/final session=GLM on the same explicit GLM request
deterministic shared MiniMax + explicit GLM and shared GLM + explicit Qwen regressions
explicit unknown model regression proving no unrelated shared authority is persisted
no-model M60 inheritance regressions proving compatibility remains
g3.recovery_or_reason: If an explicit model cannot be canonicalized, creation persists no override and the existing per-call route reports model availability truthfully. If no model is supplied, existing shared-current inheritance remains available.

g4.rollback: Revert the corrective commit and, if deployed, publish/restart through the managed service-control generation. No persisted schema migration is required.
verification: post-deploy canary requiring session.created, wire provider, request.usage and final session to agree on the same explicit model while peer sessions remain unchanged
